title: Long Method / Excessive Function Length
content: Methods or functions exceeding 30-40 lines of code frequently violate the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP). They are difficult to comprehend, test, and maintain, and they often hide subtle control-flow bugs or security validation gaps.
secure_example:
def process_order(user_id: str, order_request: OrderRequest) -> OrderReceipt:
    validate_cart(order_request.cart_items)
    total = calculate_order_total(order_request.cart_items, order_request.discount_code)
    payment = charge_payment(user_id, total, order_request.payment_info)
    order = record_order(user_id, order_request, payment.transaction_id)
    dispatch_order_confirmation(user_id, order)
    return OrderReceipt(order_id=order.id, status='CONFIRMED')
remediation_guidelines: Extract smaller cohesive functions with well-defined parameters and single responsibilities.
Keep method lengths ideally under 25-30 lines.

title: High Cyclomatic Complexity & Deep Nesting
content: Cyclomatic complexity measures the number of linearly independent paths through program source code. High complexity (> 10) and deep indentation levels (> 3 levels of nested if/for/while blocks) exponentially increase bug frequency and obscure security logic.
remediation_guidelines: Use return-early guard clauses to eliminate nested indentation.
Break complex compound conditionals into descriptive helper functions.
Aim for cyclomatic complexity scores below 10 per method.

title: God Class / Bloated Component
content: A God Class accumulates excessive duties, manages too many disparate concerns, and aggregates dozens of methods and state variables. This makes unit testing nearly impossible and encourages tight coupling across an application.
remediation_guidelines: Apply the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) to decompose large classes.
Group cohesive operations into domain-specific service objects or modules.

title: Missing Docstrings and Code Documentation (PEP 257 / Javadoc)
content: Public functions, classes, and methods lacking docstrings impede code understandability, API discoverability, and maintainability (CWE-1078). In Python, adhere to PEP 257 structured docstrings detailing arguments, return types, and exceptions raised. In Java, declare standard Javadoc blocks (@param, @return, @throws).
secure_example:
def authenticate_user(username: str, password: str) -> Optional[User]:
    """Authenticates user credentials against the secure identity store.

    Args:
        username: Unique account identifier.
        password: Plaintext password candidate.

    Returns:
        User object if credentials match; otherwise None.

    Raises:
        AuthenticationError: If identity provider is unreachable.
    """
    return verify(username, password)
remediation_guidelines: Add structured docstrings adhering to PEP 257 (Python) or Javadoc (Java).
Explicitly document all function arguments, return types, and potential raised exceptions.
